Synopsis:
Trump aides are strategically attempting to contain the US-Iran conflict before November 2026 midterm elections, fearing the unpopular war (63% disapproval) will hurt Republican majorities. The administration is shifting toward economic pressure — sanctions and a naval blockade — rather than kinetic action, while military readiness is strained by depleted munitions stockpiles. Escalation risk remains high as both sides continue tit-for-tat strikes, Trump's rhetoric is volatile, Gulf allies are urging de-escalation, and China is undermining the sanctions campaign. The November electoral calendar is effectively driving US Iran strategy.
